title: When Democratic Newcomers Challenge the Party Line

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Alarm over the election of Donald Trump inspired dozens of first-time candidates to run for
sentences.zh: 对唐纳德·特朗普当选的恐慌，激励了数十位首次参选的候选人在今年秋天竞选

sentences.en: Congress this fall.
sentences.zh: 国会议员。

sentences.en: Why those candidates are now a problem for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 为什么这些候选人现在成了民主党的一个问题。

sentences.en: It's Friday,
sentences.zh: 今天是6月1日，星期五。

sentences.en: June 1St. 2018 midterm election season is officially underway, kicked off in Texas.
sentences.zh: 2018年中期选举季正式拉开帷幕，从德克萨斯州开始。

sentences.en: Leland Bittert's digging in.
sentences.zh: 利兰·比特正在深入调查。

sentences.en: He's got that story for us tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚他为我们带来了相关报道。

sentences.en: Hey, Leland.
sentences.zh: 嘿，利兰。

sentences.en: Hey, Shannon.
sentences.zh: 嘿，香农。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: You know, even The Washington Post says Democrats face an identity crisis that they will have to solve if they want a blue wave to sweep America in 2018.
sentences.zh: 你知道，连《华盛顿邮报》都说，如果民主党想在2018年掀起蓝色浪潮席卷美国，他们就必须解决自身面临的身份危机。

sentences.en: I think one of the biggest untold stories in Washington, the Democratic Party is going through its own identity situation, crisis, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我认为华盛顿最不为人知的故事之一，就是民主党正在经历一场身份认同的困境、危机，随便怎么称呼吧。

sentences.en: But increasingly, those same Democrats are voicing concerns that the party hasn't figured out its message or a strategy.
sentences.zh: 但越来越多的民主党人表示，该党还没有找到明确的信息或策略。

sentences.en: It's not enough just to be against Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 仅仅反对唐纳德·特朗普是不够的。

sentences.en: The Democrats need a message and they need to bring something more to the table and not just being the anti-Trump party.
sentences.zh: 民主党需要一个明确的主张，他们需要拿出更多实质性的东西，而不仅仅是做一个反特朗普的政党。

sentences.en: Here's my question.
sentences.zh: 这是我的问题。

sentences.en: I ask it every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都在问。

sentences.en: What exactly is the party's message?
sentences.zh: 这个党的政纲到底是什么？

sentences.en: I came over to this country when I was a nine-year-old.
sentences.zh: 我九岁时来到这个国家。

sentences.en: I was part of the orphan airlift out of Vietnam during the last days of the fall of Saigon.
sentences.zh: 在西贡陷落的最后几天里，我是从越南撤离的孤儿空运计划的一员。

sentences.en: My parents had brought us to an orphanage.
sentences.zh: 我的父母把我们送到了孤儿院。

sentences.en: They were absolutely convinced that that was the only way that we were going to be able to survive the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 他们坚信那是我们能在战争结束时幸存下来的唯一途径。

sentences.en: And with my three siblings from the age of 10 down to the age of four, we were brought on to one of the last flights out of Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我和三个兄弟姐妹，年龄从4岁到10岁不等，被送上了离开越南的最后一批航班之一。

sentences.en: This flight that had orphans as well as handicapped children.
sentences.zh: 那架飞机上既有孤儿，也有残疾儿童。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: What was that flight like for you?
sentences.zh: 那次飞行对你来说是什么样的？

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: You know, the flight coming to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，飞往美国的航班

sentences.en: was the most scary and the most painful experience of my life.
sentences.zh: 是我一生中最可怕、最痛苦的经历。

sentences.en: I had never been on a plane and there I was on this plane with a lot of children and it was a long flight and I was, you know, away from my parents for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未坐过飞机，当时我身处这架载满孩子的飞机上，飞行时间很长，而且你知道，我第一次离开父母。

sentences.en: So it was such a scary experience.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一次非常可怕的经历。

sentences.en: And because of that, you know, one of the American soldiers actually carried me off the plane.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，你知道，其中一位美国士兵实际上是抱着我走下飞机的。

sentences.en: And it was this action of this American soldier who really gave me my incredible gratitude to this country.
sentences.zh: 正是这位美国士兵的举动，让我对这个国家产生了无比的感激之情。

sentences.en: He truly was a savior in my mind.
sentences.zh: 在我心中，他确实是一位救世主。

sentences.en: For someone to care and comfort children, I think that that is the best thing to do in the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为，关心和安慰孩子是世界上最美好的事情。

sentences.en: And that's when I decided I was going to be a pediatrician.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，我决定要成为一名儿科医生。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Tending to kids as that Marine did to you.
sentences.zh: 像那位海军陆战队员照顾你一样照顾孩子们。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: My contraint is running for Congress in California's 39th district.
sentences.zh: 我的选区正在竞选加州第39选区的国会议员。

sentences.en: I thought about running for office the day after the election of November of 2016.
sentences.zh: 我在2016年11月选举后的第二天就考虑过参选。

sentences.en: It was such a painful night.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常痛苦的夜晚。

sentences.en: My mom and I and my daughter, we were so excited to go and vote for the first female president.
sentences.zh: 我和我妈妈还有我女儿，我们当时非常兴奋地去投票，希望能选出第一位女总统。

sentences.en: And the outcome was just so unexpectedly devastating and painful that I didn't want to get up the next day.
sentences.zh: 但结果却出乎意料地令人崩溃和痛苦，以至于第二天我都不想起床。

sentences.en: But I did.
sentences.zh: 但我还是起床了。

sentences.en: I came in and one of the first patients I saw that day was a five-year-old with a brain tumor.
sentences.zh: 我上班后见到的第一批病人之一，是一个患有脑瘤的五岁孩子。

sentences.en: This is a mom who is a nail salon worker.
sentences.zh: 这位母亲是一名美甲店员工。

sentences.en: They didn't have any health insurance.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何医疗保险。

sentences.en: And they were finally able to get the subsidies through the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 他们最终通过《平价医疗法案》获得了补贴。

sentences.en: And so she was getting her treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以她正在接受治疗。

sentences.en: She had had her surgery.
sentences.zh: 她已经做完了手术。

sentences.en: She was doing her chemo.
sentences.zh: 她正在进行化疗。

sentences.en: And mom had this petrified look on her face.
sentences.zh: 那位母亲脸上带着一种惊恐的表情。

sentences.en: And I looked at her mom.
sentences.zh: 我看着她的母亲。

sentences.en: Both of us just burst out in tears.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都忍不住泪流满面。

sentences.en: I knew that there was going to be a constant effort to dismantle the Affordable Care Act and take
sentences.zh: 我知道，肯定会有人不断试图废除《平价医疗法案》，并夺走

sentences.en: away health insurance for so many of the families in my community and all the patients that I see on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我社区中许多家庭以及我每天诊治的所有病人的医疗保险。

sentences.en: You know, I knew that this was going to impact our community tremendously.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我知道这将对我们的社区产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: That's when I really decided to fight.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我真正决定要站出来抗争。

sentences.en: So you would say that it was your work as a pediatrician and the fact that President-elect Trump at that moment had talked so much about repealing the
sentences.zh: 所以你会说，正是你作为儿科医生的工作，以及当时当选总统特朗普谈论了太多关于废除

sentences.en: Affordable Care Act, which would affect your patients, that ultimately caused you to run for office.
sentences.zh: 《平价医疗法案》的事，这会影响你的病人，最终促使你决定参选。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It was a direct reaction to the outcome of the 2016 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 这是对2016年总统大选结果的直接反应。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine a candidate who more fully embodies the backlash against President Trump than Dr. Tran.
sentences.zh: 很难想象还有哪位候选人比陈医生更能体现对特朗普总统的强烈抵制。

sentences.en: Alex Burns covers national politics for The Times.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·伯恩斯负责《纽约时报》的全国政治报道。

sentences.en: She is an immigrant.
sentences.zh: 她是一位移民。

sentences.en: She's a refugee.
sentences.zh: 她是一位难民。

sentences.en: She's a woman.
sentences.zh: 她是一位女性。

sentences.en: She's a person of color.
sentences.zh: 她是一位有色人种。

sentences.en: She's a self-made success story in medicine.
sentences.zh: 她在医学领域白手起家，是一个成功的故事。

sentences.en: And she's someone who's not worked in politics before.
sentences.zh: 而且她以前从未从事过政治工作。

sentences.en: Meet Dr. Maikon Tran, an Orange County, California, a pediatrician, hoping to unseat 13-term Republican Congressman Ed Royce in the midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 来认识一下加州橙县的儿科医生迈肯·陈医生，她希望在中期选举中击败已连任13届的共和党国会议员埃德·罗伊斯，

sentences.en: focusing her platform on health care.
sentences.zh: 她的竞选纲领重点是医疗保健。

sentences.en: So in the battle for control of Congress, Democrats need to pick up 23 seats nationwide in order to win a majority in the chamber.
sentences.zh: 在争夺国会控制权的战斗中，民主党需要在全国范围内增加23个席位才能赢得众议院的多数席位。

sentences.en: In California alone, there are seven Republican-held districts that Hillary Clinton carried in the presidential race.
sentences.zh: 仅在加利福尼亚州，就有七个由共和党控制的选区在总统大选中支持了希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: That makes it the single most important state on the map in terms of whether Democrats can build a congressional majority.
sentences.zh: 这使得它成为地图上最重要的州，决定了民主党能否在国会建立多数优势。

sentences.en: And the seat that Dr. Tran is seeking is one of those seven.
sentences.zh: 而陈医生竞选的席位正是这七个席位之一。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We need a doctor to fix this broken health care system.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一位医生来修复这个破碎的医疗体系。

sentences.en: Who could be better than a practicing physician who also is a patient?
sentences.zh: 还有谁比一位既是医生又是病人的执业医师更合适呢？

sentences.en: She's not for single payer.
sentences.zh: 她不支持全民医保。

sentences.en: She's like strongly anti-Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 她强烈反对佩洛西。

sentences.en: She has reservations about raising taxes on businesses.
sentences.zh: 她对增加企业税持保留意见。

sentences.en: In a lot of ways, she's a couple sticks to the center.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，她更倾向于中间派。

sentences.en: The 39th district is just a quintessential anti-Trump, historically Republican district.
sentences.zh: 第39选区是一个典型的反特朗普、历史上属于共和党的选区。

sentences.en: It's anchored in Orange County.
sentences.zh: 它位于橙县。

sentences.en: It includes Richard Nixon's birthplace.
sentences.zh: 它包括理查德·尼克松的出生地。

sentences.en: This is a place where for decades, your sort of country club Republicans made this a solidly right-of-center seat.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，这里一直是那种乡村俱乐部共和党人稳固的中间偏右选区。

sentences.en: But President
sentences.zh: 但特朗普

sentences.en: Trump lost the district handily.
sentences.zh: 总统在该选区惨败。

sentences.en: So this seat is held by Republicans, but it sounds like it could go either way.
sentences.zh: 所以这个席位虽然由共和党人把持，但听起来两党都有机会。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is a district in transition.
sentences.zh: 这是一个处于转型期的选区。

sentences.en: This is one of these areas of the country.
sentences.zh: 这是该国这类地区之一。

sentences.en: It's a booming suburb with growing communities of Hispanic and Asian American voters and affluent whites who have never been particularly enthralled with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 这是一个蓬勃发展的郊区，拥有越来越多的西班牙裔和亚裔选民，以及从未对特朗普总统特别着迷的富裕白人。

sentences.en: But even though the district is unfriendly to President Trump, it is not a liberal area.
sentences.zh: 但尽管该选区对特朗普总统不友好，它并不是一个自由派地区。

sentences.en: And it's really tough to beat an incumbent member of Congress, especially an incumbent as prominent as Ed Royce.
sentences.zh: 击败现任国会议员非常困难，尤其是像埃德·罗伊斯这样显赫的现任议员。

sentences.en: He's the chairman of the
sentences.zh: 他是众议院

sentences.en: House Foreign Relations Committee.
sentences.zh: 外交委员会主席。

sentences.en: He has deep relationships with the Asian American community in his district.
sentences.zh: 他在选区的亚裔社区拥有深厚的关系。

sentences.en: He's not a Trump Republican.
sentences.zh: 他不是特朗普派的共和党人。

sentences.en: So this guy is not going to be a pushover even in a tough political climate for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在对共和党不利的政治气候下，这家伙也不是好对付的。

sentences.en: But if anyone has a shot early on, it's a candidate who looks exactly like her.
sentences.zh: 但如果有人有机会，那就是像她这样的候选人。

sentences.en: A lot of people stayed out because it was seen as an impossibility.
sentences.zh: 很多人因为觉得不可能获胜而选择了观望。

sentences.en: But I have been listening to the children and their families in this district for 25 years, the same amount of time that our current congressman has been in Congress ignoring them.
sentences.zh: 但我已经倾听这个选区的孩子和他们的家庭25年了，这和我们现任国会议员在国会忽视他们的时间一样长。

sentences.en: And I saw myself as the little lady that was going to slay the giant.
sentences.zh: 我把自己看作是那个要打倒巨人的小女子。

sentences.en: You know, I was getting all of the endorsements from women's groups.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我得到了所有妇女团体的背书。

sentences.en: I was getting all the endorsements from the Asian American groups and the science groups.
sentences.zh: 我得到了所有亚裔团体和科学团体的背书。

sentences.en: And then I was raising money.
sentences.zh: 而且我还在筹集资金。

sentences.en: So I was very, very happy with where the campaign was going.
sentences.zh: 所以我对竞选的进展感到非常非常高兴。

sentences.en: Then Ed Royce decides he's not running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 然后埃德·罗伊斯决定不再寻求连任。

sentences.en: California Republican Congressman Ed Royce announced he won't seek re-election this year.
sentences.zh: 加州共和党国会议员埃德·罗伊斯宣布他今年不会寻求连任。

sentences.en: This sends a shock through both parties.
sentences.zh: 这让两党都感到震惊。

sentences.en: Republicans were counting on him to hold the seat.
sentences.zh: 共和党人指望他守住这个席位。

sentences.en: And suddenly you have a free-for-all on the Democratic side.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，民主党这边陷入了一场混战。

sentences.en: After news of Royce's retirement, the Cook Political Report shifted the race from lean Republican to lean Democrat.
sentences.zh: 在罗伊斯退休的消息传出后，《库克政治报告》将该选区的选情从“倾向共和党”调整为“倾向民主党”。

sentences.en: They don't just have one or two credible candidates in an underdog race.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是在一场不被看好的竞选中有一两个可靠的候选人。

sentences.en: Then they have everybody who wants to run for this sudden open seat.
sentences.zh: 现在每个人都想竞选这个突然空出的席位。

sentences.en: In several of the most competitive districts, there are so many Democrats on the ballot that there's a chance that they could all splinter the vote.
sentences.zh: 在几个竞争最激烈的选区，选票上有太多的民主党人，他们有可能分散选票。

sentences.en: And in California, if everybody runs, then that primary gets really complicated.
sentences.zh: 而在加州，如果每个人都参选，那么初选就会变得非常复杂。

sentences.en: The state has a set of rules where you don't run in a Democratic primary and a Republican primary.
sentences.zh: 该州有一套规则，你不能只参加民主党初选或共和党初选。

sentences.en: Like in most places.
sentences.zh: 像大多数地方一样。

sentences.en: Like in most places.
sentences.zh: 像大多数地方一样。

sentences.en: Everybody runs in the same primary.
sentences.zh: 每个人都参加同一场初选。

sentences.en: And the top two finishers, regardless of the party, advance the general election.
sentences.zh: 无论党派如何，得票最高的前两名进入大选。

sentences.en: Now suddenly you have half a dozen or more Democrats, half a dozen Republicans.
sentences.zh: 现在突然间你有六个或更多的民主党人，六个共和党人。

sentences.en: And if the Democrats carve up their votes too finely, you could have a Republican on Republican general election.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人把选票分得太细，你可能会看到一场共和党对阵共和党的大选。

sentences.en: So you could end up with a general election in which there are two Republicans and zero Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以你最终可能会迎来一场只有两名共和党人、没有民主党人的大选。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what does that mean for Dr. Tran?
sentences.zh: 那么这对陈医生意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means that suddenly she's in the position of fighting for the support and attention of
sentences.zh: 这意味着她突然处于必须争取支持和关注的境地，

sentences.en: Democrats who she thought would be with her from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而这些民主党人她本以为从一开始就会支持她。

sentences.en: Democrats in this district now have too much of a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这个选区的民主党人现在面临着“好事多磨”的困境。

sentences.en: They have a number of candidates, all of whom have interesting life stories and interesting theories of how you win that district competing against each other for the
sentences.zh: 他们有许多候选人，每个人都有有趣的人生故事和有趣的获胜理论，他们正在为

sentences.en: same set of Democratic votes.
sentences.zh: 同一批民主党选票而相互竞争。

sentences.en: And the National Democratic Party decides they've got to do something to make sure that they don't end up locked out of the general election.
sentences.zh: 全国民主党决定他们必须采取行动，确保自己不会在大选中被拒之门外。

sentences.en: So what do they do?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是怎么做的呢？

sentences.en: So once the dust has settled a little bit, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee runs a set of polls in the district.
sentences.zh: 在局势稍微平稳后，民主党国会竞选委员会在该选区进行了一系列民意调查。

sentences.en: They go to each of the candidates running and ask them to write up a positive biography about their candidates.
sentences.zh: 他们找到每一位参选人，要求他们为自己的候选人撰写一份正面的传记。

sentences.en: Then they go into the field.
sentences.zh: 然后他们进入实地调查。

sentences.en: They ask voters, who do you like?
sentences.zh: 他们询问选民：你喜欢谁？

sentences.en: And they want to see whose story resonates the most in this district.
sentences.zh: 他们想看看谁的故事在这个选区最能引起共鸣。

sentences.en: The conclusion that they draw from that poll is that Dr. Tran's support did not move enough for them to believe that she could make the general election.
sentences.zh: 他们从民调中得出的结论是，陈博士的支持率提升幅度不足以让他们相信她能进入大选。

sentences.en: We got a call from the National Party and we were asked to not continue in the campaign.
sentences.zh: 我们接到了全国党的电话，被要求停止竞选活动。

sentences.en: It was clearly stated that I would be a spoiler if I continue.
sentences.zh: 他们明确表示，如果我继续参选，我就是一个搅局者。

sentences.en: What did you say when they made this request?
sentences.zh: 当他们提出这个要求时，你是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, the first phrase that came out of my mouth was, who gives you the right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我脱口而出的第一句话是：谁给了你们这个权利？

sentences.en: And then secondly was, how dare you?
sentences.zh: 第二句是：你们怎么敢这样？

sentences.en: How dare you ask somebody who's been running for more than, how about that time, six months, somebody who has raised the most money, the only working mom, the only qualified woman,
sentences.zh: 你们怎么敢要求一个已经参选了——当时算起来有六个月了——一个筹款最多、唯一的职场妈妈、唯一的合格女性、

sentences.en: the only doctor?
sentences.zh: 唯一的医生的人退选？

sentences.en: How is that possible that I'm not a good candidate?
sentences.zh: 我怎么可能不是一个好的候选人？

sentences.en: But it didn't end there.
sentences.zh: 但事情并没有就此结束。

sentences.en: Then I got calls from congressional members telling me that I should drop out of the race.
sentences.zh: 后来我接到了国会议员的电话，告诉我应该退出竞选。

sentences.en: Many of these congressional members were the ones who actually talked to me about running.
sentences.zh: 这些国会议员中，有许多人当初正是劝我参选的人。

sentences.en: I've even had a in-person visit as well from one of the congressional members and he told me about the data.
sentences.zh: 我甚至还亲自接待了一位国会议员，他跟我谈到了数据。

sentences.en: He said, the numbers aren't there.
sentences.zh: 他说，数据不支持你。

sentences.en: You know the data.
sentences.zh: 你知道这些数据的。

sentences.en: You should not continue.
sentences.zh: 你不应该继续下去了。

sentences.en: I was respectful, but I said, I absolutely am going to stay in.
sentences.zh: 我表现得很尊重，但我说，我绝对会坚持到底。

sentences.en: And I was determined to prove them wrong.
sentences.zh: 我决心证明他们是错的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Democrats will look to regain a majority in the House of Representatives this November, and they can take a major step towards doing so on June 5th when primary voters in
sentences.zh: 民主党人希望在今年11月夺回众议院多数席位，而6月5日加州的初选选民投票，

sentences.en: California head to the polls.
sentences.zh: 将是他们实现这一目标的重要一步。

sentences.en: Alex, are you surprised that this grassroots candidate with no political experience basically told the national Democrats to go fly a kite?
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，这位毫无政治经验的草根候选人基本上让全国民主党人“滚一边去”，你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: I'm actually not surprised.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不惊讶。

sentences.en: And it's one of the things that's striking and in some ways refreshing about this campaign is that one of the challenges for national Democrats is that so many new candidates,
sentences.zh: 这场竞选最引人注目，在某些方面也令人耳目一新的地方在于，全国民主党人面临的挑战之一是，许多新候选人，

sentences.en: these people who they're celebrating as part of a resistance to President Trump, have no particular stake in the institutions of the national party.
sentences.zh: 那些被他们誉为反抗特朗普总统的一部分的人，与全国党的体制并没有什么特殊的利益关联。

sentences.en: That Dr. Tran is not the only political newcomer who isn't worried about what Democrats in Washington will think of her in one year or five years,
sentences.zh: 陈博士并不是唯一一个不担心华盛顿的民主党人在一年或五年后会如何看待她的政治新人，

sentences.en: and they're not worried about staying on the right side of people who are the traditional power brokers in the party.
sentences.zh: 他们也不担心如何讨好党内传统的权力掮客。

sentences.en: And they can't be controlled in the same way as conventional politicians.
sentences.zh: 他们无法像传统政客那样被控制。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In many ways, they have contempt for the system.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，他们对这个体制充满蔑视。

sentences.en: They see the system as having failed in
sentences.zh: 他们认为这个体制在
2016年失败了。

sentences.en: They see the Democratic Party as having failed in 2016.
sentences.zh: 他们认为民主党在2016年失败了。

sentences.en: And part of the reason why they're running in the first place is they see the results of the party institutions and they say, I can do better than that.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以参选，部分原因在于他们看到了党内机构的结果，并说：我能做得更好。

sentences.en: So tell us about the Democrats' favorite choice in this race.
sentences.zh: 那么，请告诉我们民主党在这场竞选中青睐的选择。

sentences.en: According to the national party's poll, of the candidates who have a shot at making the general election, their best chance is a man named Gil Cisneros.
sentences.zh: 根据全国党的民调，在有机会进入大选的候选人中，他们胜算最大的是一个叫吉尔·西斯内罗斯的人。

sentences.en: Leaders must lead with their actions as well as their words.
sentences.zh: 领导者不仅要用言语，更要用行动来引领。

sentences.en: It's a lesson I learned during my years of service in the Navy.
sentences.zh: 这是我在海军服役期间学到的教训。

sentences.en: He's a former Republican who has acknowledged that he voted for John McCain in 2008 over Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 他是一位前共和党人，曾承认在2008年投票支持约翰·麦凯恩，而不是巴拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: He has sort of the ultimate political Cinderella story of having been just a regular guy who didn't even
sentences.zh: 他有着终极的政治版“灰姑娘”故事，他原本只是一个普通人，甚至不怎么

sentences.en: play the lottery regularly and then one day bought 10 tickets and one of them earned him 300 million dollars.
sentences.zh: 买彩票，结果有一天买了10张，其中一张让他赢得了3亿美元。

sentences.en: So when fortune struck, I knew it was my duty to do what was right, to help those who needed it most.
sentences.zh: 所以当好运降临时，我知道我有责任做正确的事，去帮助那些最需要帮助的人。

sentences.en: And after that happened for him and his wife, they started getting engaged in
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他和妻子开始投身于

sentences.en: politics.
sentences.zh: 政治。

sentences.en: They became significant political donors to Democrats at that point, including the Obama
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他们成为了民主党的重要政治捐款人，包括2012年的奥巴马

sentences.en: campaign in 2012, to the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, to any number of powerful California
sentences.zh: 竞选活动、国会西裔党团，以及许多加州有权势的

sentences.en: Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党人。

sentences.en: I'm tired of politicians who sold out to special interests.
sentences.zh: 我厌倦了那些向特殊利益集团出卖灵魂的政客。

sentences.en: This is our government and it needs to work for us.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的政府，它必须为我们服务。

sentences.en: That's why I'm running for Congress and I won't take corporate PAC money.
sentences.zh: 这就是我竞选国会议员的原因，我不会接受企业政治行动委员会的钱。

sentences.en: I'm Gil Cisneros and I approve this message because leading by example is how we fix Washington.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·西斯内罗斯，我批准这条信息，因为以身作则是我们修复华盛顿的方式。

sentences.en: Dr. Tran, why do you think the Democratic Party decided to back Gil Cisneros over you?
sentences.zh: 陈博士，你认为民主党为什么决定支持吉尔·西斯内罗斯而不是你？

sentences.en: The party decided to go with a candidate that has the most money because I think it is using the same traditional way of assessing success of a congressional campaign.
sentences.zh: 党决定选择一个最有钱的候选人，因为我认为他们还在用评估国会竞选成功的传统方式。

sentences.en: And that's what to me, it's sad that the Democratic Party didn't learn the lessons of the 2016 election, that politics has to be done differently.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，令人悲哀的是民主党没有吸取2016年大选的教训，即政治必须以不同的方式进行。

sentences.en: It cannot be done in the same traditional ways, using the same parameters that we would use to predict outcome.
sentences.zh: 不能再用同样的传统方式，用我们过去预测结果的那些参数来衡量。

sentences.en: Well, but wouldn't the National Democratic Party say that they are trying to learn the lessons of the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但全国民主党人难道不会说他们正在努力吸取2016年大选的教训吗？

sentences.en: And one of those lessons is that Donald Trump appealed to a huge swath of the American public and therefore the Democrats may need to run candidates who can
sentences.zh: 其中一个教训是，唐纳德·特朗普吸引了美国公众的很大一部分，因此民主党可能需要推出能够

sentences.en: appeal to some of those same people.
sentences.zh: 吸引其中一些人的候选人。

sentences.en: I don't think that's what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们是在那样做。

sentences.en: I really believe that the
sentences.zh: 我真的相信

sentences.en: Party wants to win so badly that they are picking the easier, the more convenient candidate.
sentences.zh: 党太想赢了，以至于他们选择了更容易、更方便的候选人。

sentences.en: It's not about my politics.
sentences.zh: 这与我的政治立场无关。

sentences.en: She is right that it's not about appealing to Trump voters.
sentences.zh: 她说得对，这与吸引特朗普选民无关。

sentences.en: The complexity to it is that it is about appealing to moderate voters in a district where it is very, very expensive to run a political campaign.
sentences.zh: 复杂之处在于，这关乎在一个竞选成本非常、非常昂贵的选区吸引温和派选民。

sentences.en: So this is a district in the Los Angeles media market, one of the most expensive places
sentences.zh: 这是一个位于洛杉矶媒体市场的选区，是美国广告投放

sentences.en: to advertise in the United States, full of people who are open to voting Democratic in 2018, but
sentences.zh: 最昂贵的地方之一，这里的人们在2018年愿意投票给民主党，但

sentences.en: probably haven't done that a whole lot in the paSt. So Democrats are looking for a candidate who can
sentences.zh: 过去可能并没有这样做过。所以民主党人正在寻找一个能够

sentences.en: raise a ton of money or write themselves a check for a ton of money and then go on the air with an
sentences.zh: 筹集大量资金，或者自己掏腰包开出一张巨额支票，然后通过广告

sentences.en: argument that can convince those folks that, yeah, come on in, the water's fine, you can vote Democratic.
sentences.zh: 去说服那些人：是的，来吧，水温正好，你们可以投票给民主党。

sentences.en: Fundraising is such a big part of a congressional campaign.
sentences.zh: 筹款是国会竞选的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: We're told constantly to just stay on the phone, reach out to the donors, get the money, get the fundraising going.
sentences.zh: 我们不断被告知要一直打电话，联系捐款人，筹集资金，让竞选筹款运转起来。

sentences.en: I was sitting in my garage making those phone calls.
sentences.zh: 我当时坐在车库里打那些电话。

sentences.en: And after a few rejections, I was just on the ground in tears, crying.
sentences.zh: 在几次被拒绝后，我瘫倒在地，泪流满面。

sentences.en: And here my mom, she walked into the garage, saw me on the ground crying.
sentences.zh: 这时我妈妈走进车库，看到我瘫在地上哭。

sentences.en: And she looked at me and she said, do you want me to give you a little bit of the pieces of gold that I had kept during my escape from Vietnam?
sentences.zh: 她看着我说：你想让我给你一点我在逃离越南时保留的碎金子吗？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: During the escape, those who had any money would have little pieces of gold hidden all over to try to get out of the country and then to try to build new lives.
sentences.zh: 在逃亡期间，那些有钱的人会把碎金子藏在各处，试图逃离这个国家，然后试图建立新的生活。

sentences.en: But here's my elderly mom telling me that her last piece of gold, she would give it to me so that her daughter, a refugee, could be running for Congress.
sentences.zh: 但现在我年迈的母亲告诉我，她要把最后一点金子给我，好让她的女儿，一个难民，能够竞选国会议员。

sentences.en: And that made me cry even more.
sentences.zh: 这让我哭得更厉害了。

sentences.en: I mean, I just got even louder with my sobbing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的啜泣声变得更大了。

sentences.en: My poor mom, you know, with her last little flake of gold was going to help her daughter
sentences.zh: 我可怜的妈妈，你知道，她要用她最后的一点金子来帮助她的女儿

sentences.en: run for Congress.
sentences.zh: 竞选国会议员。

sentences.en: She has struggled to put together the money that her opponents have on the Democratic side.
sentences.zh: 她一直在努力筹集与民主党内对手相当的资金。

sentences.en: She is a wealthy candidate.
sentences.zh: 她是一位富有的候选人。

sentences.en: She's put in hundreds of thousands of dollars of her own money.
sentences.zh: 她投入了数十万美元的个人资金。

sentences.en: And she's also raised a decent bit of money for the race.
sentences.zh: 她也为竞选筹集了一笔不错的资金。

sentences.en: She's raised more than her most important
sentences.zh: 她筹集的资金比她最重要的

sentences.en: Democratic competitors.
sentences.zh: 民主党竞争对手还要多。

sentences.en: But they've not really been trying to take other people's money.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有真正试图去拿别人的钱。

sentences.en: They've just been writing themselves bigger and bigger checks out of their personal fortunes.
sentences.zh: 他们只是从个人财富中给自己开出越来越大的支票。

sentences.en: So Dr. Tran may be right that this is not so much about politics as it is about the strength of her candidacy.
sentences.zh: 所以陈博士可能是对的，这与其说是政治问题，不如说是她竞选实力的问题。

sentences.en: And the strength of her candidacy in the eyes of the Democratic Party nationally is, do you have enough money to win?
sentences.zh: 而在全国民主党人眼中，她竞选实力的衡量标准是：你有足够的钱赢吗？

sentences.en: And they've concluded that she really doesn't.
sentences.zh: 他们得出的结论是，她确实没有。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So one of the dominant narratives of this campaign is that the Democratic Party is torn and conflicted about what it should be in this election.
sentences.zh: 所以这场竞选的主导叙事之一是，民主党对于这次选举中自己应该成为什么样子感到纠结和矛盾。

sentences.en: Should it be about liberal policies and identity?
sentences.zh: 它应该关注自由派政策和身份认同吗？

sentences.en: Or should it be about pursuing the kinds of voters who supported President Trump?
sentences.zh: 还是应该关注争取那些支持特朗普总统的选民？

sentences.en: And you're saying that this race in California doesn't seem to be about that choice.
sentences.zh: 而你说加州的这场竞选似乎并不是关于这个选择。

sentences.en: There's no question that it's an enormous political opportunity for Democrats to gain a seat.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这对民主党来说是一个巨大的政治机会，可以赢得一个席位。

sentences.en: But I don't know that you're going to see the new Democratic identity forged in Orange County.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道你是否会在橙县看到新的民主党身份认同的形成。

sentences.en: That may be forged elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 那可能是在其他地方形成的。

sentences.en: Look, the good news for Democrats is that there's enough political opportunity on the map for them to win control of the House without settling their identity in a monolithic way.
sentences.zh: 听着，对民主党来说好消息是，地图上有足够的政治机会让他们赢得众议院控制权，而无需以单一的方式确定他们的身份。

sentences.en: The bad news for
sentences.zh: 对

sentences.en: Democrats is that they may well come out of this election doing very well on a case-by-case basis, but not really resolving their identity crisis at all.
sentences.zh: 民主党来说坏消息是，他们很可能在这次选举中个案表现得很好，但并没有真正解决他们的身份危机。

sentences.en: In other words, Democrats may win a majority, but it won't be really clear what that majority stands for.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，民主党可能会赢得多数席位，但并不清楚这个多数派代表什么。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: You could have candidates like Gil Cisneros or like Dr. Tran serving alongside
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到像吉尔·西斯内罗斯或陈博士这样的候选人，与

sentences.en: Democrats who are pro-gun and pro-border wall.
sentences.zh: 支持拥枪和支持边境墙的民主党人并肩工作。

sentences.en: And it's anyone's guess what that party would actually do with its power.
sentences.zh: 谁也猜不到这个党在掌握权力后会真正做什么。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: When will we have an answer to the question of who the Democrats are more broadly?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候才能得到关于民主党到底是什么的答案？

sentences.en: To me, that question is probably going to have to wait until 2020.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这个问题可能要等到2020年。

sentences.en: The next presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 下一次总统竞选。

sentences.en: Until the party decides on a person and a message and a set of ideas embodied in a single standard bearer.
sentences.zh: 直到该党确定一个人、一个信息以及一套由单一旗手体现的理念。

sentences.en: I think you're going to see a lot of sort of all over the map primary elections and
sentences.zh: 我认为你会看到很多各地的初选，以及

sentences.en: very sort of opportunistic strategic decisions by the national party about who do we need to recruit to win in front of this very specific set of voters.
sentences.zh: 全国党在战略上非常投机的决定，关于我们需要招募谁来赢得这些特定选民的支持。

sentences.en: But that strategy you're outlining, I wonder how demoralizing that must be for all of these candidates like Dr. Tran who felt that they were

sentences.en: fulfilling the fantasy of the party to enter political life after the election of Donald Trump only to be

sentences.en: Look, I think that's been a really, really bracing experience for a whole bunch of the candidates,

sentences.en: especially in California, where these just tactical, structural, cold political considerations are such a dominant priority in Democratic politics.
sentences.zh: 这种把身份认同问题推迟到以后解决，在以后某个时间点再决定民主党是谁的策略，

sentences.en: Is this strategy of kind of kicking the identity can down the road, resolving the question of who the Democrats are at some later point?
sentences.zh: 是否危险？

sentences.en: Is that dangerous?
sentences.zh: 因为它是否冒着让民主党更难在2020年以有效方式弄清自己是谁的风险，如果他们现在不弄清楚的话？

sentences.en: Because does it risk making it harder for the Democrats to figure out who they are in an effective way for 2020 if they aren't figuring it out now?
sentences.zh: 哦，我认为毫无疑问，推迟这个问题是有风险的。

sentences.en: Oh, I think there's no question there are risks involved in pushing that question off.
sentences.zh: 你不需要看太远，看看众议院

sentences.en: And you don't need to look any further than the House

sentences.en: Republican majority to see those risks sort of carried out to full effect that Republicans ran for years
sentences.zh: 以混乱的政策纲领和一群主要因对奥巴马总统的厌恶而团结在一起的折中候选人进行竞选。

sentences.en: on a muddled platform of policies with a eclectic group of candidates united mainly by their distaste for President Obama.

sentences.en: commentator, author, and filmmaker who pled guilty in 2014 to making illegal campaign donations.
sentences.zh: 评论员、作家和电影制作人，曾于2014年承认非法竞选捐款罪。

sentences.zh: 我超额了。

sentences.en: I broke the law.
sentences.zh: 我触犯了法律。

sentences.en: D'Souza is known for controversial and unsubstantiated claims about Democrats, including the assertion that liberals were largely responsible for inspiring the September 11th

sentences.en: attacks, and that Barack Obama harbored an anti-colonial agenda aimed at weakening the U.S.

sentences.en: Obama has a dream, a dream from his father, that the sins of colonialism be set right and America be downsized.

sentences.en: In a tweet, Trump wrote that D'Souza, who received five years of probation for his illegal donations, was, quote, treated very unfairly by our government.
